purpose: BLINDED evidence packets for the independent second-pass adjudicator. This file deliberately contains NO Evaluation V2 disposition for any case; the reviewer forms an independent judgment from the excerpts alone. The sealed label file is separate.
instructionsForReviewer: For each case: read the ground-truth claim (excerpt + adjudicated description), then read each candidate representation's own excerpt and normalized semantics.
Answer per candidate: does it substantively represent the ground-truth claim? YES / PARTIAL / NO / AMBIGUOUS.
Then give ONE overall disposition for the claim: REPRESENTED / PARTIALLY_REPRESENTED / UNREPRESENTED / AMBIGUOUS / HONESTLY_UNRESOLVED / HONESTLY_UNSUPPORTED.

Structural adjacency is not evidence. A candidate sharing a section number, being a descendant or ancestor, sitting near a similar figure, or citing the same defined term does NOT represent the claim unless it asserts the same thing.
Cite the excerpt text you relied on. If the evidence is insufficient to decide, say AMBIGUOUS rather than guessing.

candidates.normalizedSemantics: OTHER_MATERIAL_SEMANTIC_DISCREPANCY: The source defines Acquired EBITDA not as a simple alias for the defined term 'EBITDA', but as a distinct metric computed by taking the EBITDA methodology and substituting every reference to 'the Company and its Restricted Subsidiaries' with 'such Acquired Entity or Business and its subsidiaries.' In other words, Acquired EBITDA is the acquired target's own stand-alone EBITDA calculated under the same formula, not the Company's consolidated EBITDA. The proposed IR instead models the calculationExpression as a bare DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE to 'EBITDA' with no substitution/scoping mechanism at all - meaning as compiled, Acquired EBITDA would literally resolve to the Company's own consolidated EBITDA rather than the acquired business's EBITDA. This is a materially different economic result: e.g., if the Company's consolidated EBITDA is $50,000,000 and a small acquired business has its own EBITDA of $5,000,000, the correct Acquired EBITDA add-back (used elsewhere, e.g., in the EBITDA definition's clause (a)(xviii)(a) pro forma add-back for recently acquired entities) should be $5,000,000, but the proposed IR's formula would instead resolve to $50,000,000, a nine-fold overstatement. Although the definition is marked sufficiency PARTIAL rather than COMPLETE, the calculationExpression itself is not marked UNSUPPORTED - it makes an affirmative (and wrong) formula assertion, which is exactly the kind of confident-but-wrong representation this review is meant to catch, distinguishing it from an honest disclosure of a gap.

candidates.normalizedSemantics:
OTHER_MATERIAL_SEMANTIC_DISCREPANCY: Section 1.01 defines a very large number of terms, many trivially representable (e.g., 'Account Debtor' means any Person obligated on an Account; 'Agreed Currency' means dollars or any Alternative Currency), and at least one - 'Acquisition' - carries real operative/entity-scope content (restricting qualifying transactions to 'any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary', with two alternative tests in clauses (a) and (b)). The retrieved context bundle even shows this definition already decomposed into CHILD_RULE nodes for clauses (a) and (b), indicating the definition was recognized as structurally significant, yet the proposed IR contains no 'Acquisition' entry whatsoever, nor entries for the great majority of other defined terms in this section. The deterministic signals corroborate this: 8 enumerated sub-clauses with 0 compiled rules, 16 proviso/exception markers with 0 recorded conditions, and 4 distinct entity-scope terms (Loan Party, Restricted Subsidiary, Borrower, etc.) with no entity-scope restriction recorded anywhere in the IR. A downstream reviewer relying on this IR for the meaning of 'Acquisition' - which gates whether a transaction by, say, an Unrestricted Subsidiary or a non-Loan-Party affiliate qualifies as a Permitted Acquisition elsewhere in the agreement - would find no representation of that entity-scope limitation at all, and could reach a different conclusion about what counts as an 'Acquisition' than the real source text supports. Because the artifact does not disclose (at an aggregate level) that its definitional coverage of Section 1.01 is only a small, seemingly arbitrary subset, this omission is not offset by an honest disclosure comparable to the individual PARTIAL/UNSUPPORTED markings on the five terms that were included.

By contrast, the individual PARTIAL/UNSUPPORTED markings on Alternate Base Rate, Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR, Adjusted Term SOFR Rate, Applicable Rate, and Available Amount each candidly disclose why the compiler could not represent the relevant calculation (MAX/SUBTRACT type-check failures, multi-column grid limitations) and are not themselves treated as findings, consistent with the principle that an honest disclosure of a real limitation is not a semantic defect. The problem flagged here is the silent, undisclosed absence of the remaining bulk of the section's definitions, several of which are simple and clearly compilable, and at least one of which (Acquisition) carries independently operative entity-scope content that the deterministic AMBIGUOUS signals specifically call out as missing.'

candidates.normalizedSemantics:
OTHER_MATERIAL_SEMANTIC_DISCREPANCY: Section 1.01 defines a very large number of terms, many trivially representable (e.g., 'Account Debtor' means any Person obligated on an Account; 'Agreed Currency' means dollars or any Alternative Currency), and at least one - 'Acquisition' - carries real operative/entity-scope content (restricting qualifying transactions to 'any Loan Party or Restricted Subsidiary', with two alternative tests in clauses (a) and (b)). The retrieved context bundle even shows this definition already decomposed into CHILD_RULE nodes for clauses (a) and (b), indicating the definition was recognized as structurally significant, yet the proposed IR contains no 'Acquisition' entry whatsoever, nor entries for the great majority of other defined terms in this section. The deterministic signals corroborate this: 8 enumerated sub-clauses with 0 compiled rules, 16 proviso/exception markers with 0 recorded conditions, and 4 distinct entity-scope terms (Loan Party, Restricted Subsidiary, Borrower, etc.) with no entity-scope restriction recorded anywhere in the IR. A downstream reviewer relying on this IR for the meaning of 'Acquisition' - which gates whether a transaction by, say, an Unrestricted Subsidiary or a non-Loan-Party affiliate qualifies as a Permitted Acquisition elsewhere in the agreement - would find no representation of that entity-scope limitation at all, and could reach a different conclusion about what counts as an 'Acquisition' than the real source text supports. Because the artifact does not disclose (at an aggregate level) that its definitional coverage of Section 1.01 is only a small, seemingly arbitrary subset, this omission is not offset by an honest disclosure comparable to the individual PARTIAL/UNSUPPORTED markings on the five terms that were included.

By contrast, the individual PARTIAL/UNSUPPORTED markings on Alternate Base Rate, Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR, Adjusted Term SOFR Rate, Applicable Rate, and Available Amount each candidly disclose why the compiler could not represent the relevant calculation (MAX/SUBTRACT type-check failures, multi-column grid limitations) and are not themselves treated as findings, consistent with the principle that an honest disclosure of a real limitation is not a semantic defect. The problem flagged here is the silent, undisclosed absence of the remaining bulk of the section's definitions, several of which are simple and clearly compilable, and at least one of which (Acquisition) carries independently operative entity-scope content that the deterministic AMBIGUOUS signals specifically call out as missing.'

cases.groundTruthSemanticDescription: Section 6.05(k) permits dispositions of assets, including Sale and Leaseback Transactions not otherwise permitted by clause (e)(ii), not permitted by any other clause (excluding Equity Interests in a Borrower, and excluding Equity Interests in a Restricted Subsidiary unless all of them are sold), provided the aggregate fair market value of assets Disposed of in reliance on this clause may not exceed, during any fiscal year of the Company, the greater of $25,000,000 and 25% of Applicable EBITDA, and provided further that (other than as set forth on Schedule 6.05) all such Dispositions must be made for fair value and for at least 75% cash consideration.

(a) No Loan Party will, nor will it permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, declare or make, or agree to declare or make, directly or indirectly,
any Restricted Payment, or incur any obligation (contingent or otherwise) to do so, except (i) each of the Borrowers may declare and pay dividends with respect to its common stock payable solely in additional shares of its common stock, and,
with respect to its preferred stock, payable solely in additional shares of such preferred stock (to the extent permitted to be issued hereunder) or in shares of its common stock, (ii) Restricted Subsidiaries may declare and pay dividends
ratably with respect to their Equity Interests, (iii) the Loan Parties may make Restricted Payments, pursuant to and in accordance with stock option plans or other benefit plans for management or employees of the Loan Parties and their
Restricted Subsidiaries, (iv) other Restricted Payments in an amount not to exceed the Available Amount immediately prior to the time of the making of such Restricted Payment, so long as at the time of making such Restricted Payment and
immediately after giving effect
cases.groundTruthSemanticDescription: General prohibition on making or agreeing to make any payment or distribution of or in respect of principal or interest on any Indebtedness, or on account of the purchase, redemption, retirement, acquisition, cancellation or termination of any Indebtedness, subject to clauses (i) through (iv).

groundTruthAdjudication.sourceStatement: authoredFromSourceOnly=true; methodologyNotes: Granularity: every lettered/roman-numbered sub-basket and exception in Article VI and every lettered clause of Sections 7.01 and 4.01 is its own unit; Articles III, V, VIII, IX, X and XI are captured at the section level with sub-clause units only where a clause carries independent operative effect (e.g. 9.02(b) sacred rights, 9.04(f)/(g), 10.01(a)/(b), 11.07(a)). In Article I only load-bearing definitions that gate capacity, ratios or entity applicability are enumerated; the remaining ~200 ordinary definitions are captured in one grouped unit, as is the benchmark-rate suite.
